h1: Chilling beer fast before guests arrive without freezing it
title: Chill beer fast without freezing it | Craft Beer School
desc: The quickest safe ways to chill beer before guests arrive: an ice, water and salt bath, the freezer with a timer and what never to do.
teaser: Guests in thirty minutes and the beer is warm. An ice bath with salt beats the freezer every time.
standfirst: Warm beer and guests on the way is a common Indian evening problem. The freezer is the obvious answer but also the riskiest. A bucket of ice, water and salt chills faster and never freezes the beer solid.
sections:
Put a can into a bucket of ice cubes and it touches the ice at only a few points. Air fills the gaps. Air is a poor conductor of heat. The can cools, but slowly.

Add water and everything changes. Water fills every gap and pulls heat out of the can across its whole surface. An ice and water bath sits at about 0 °C and chills cans far faster than ice alone. Add salt and it gets colder still, because salt lowers the freezing point of water. The bath can drop several degrees below zero while staying liquid.
The ice, water and salt bath

1. Fill a bucket, a cooler box or a clean sink with ice, then add cold water until the ice floats.
  2. Stir in a generous handful of salt, a few tablespoons per litre of water. Ordinary table salt or cheap rock salt both work.
  3. Push the cans or bottles in so they are fully submerged up to the neck.
  4. Give them a gentle turn every few minutes so cold water keeps moving around them.

As a rough guide, 330 ml cans from room temperature reach drinking temperature in about 10 to 15 minutes. Glass bottles take longer because glass is thicker and conducts heat less well. A 650 ml bottle can take 20 to 30 minutes. Check one by touch or with a thermometer rather than trusting the clock.

The freezer works, but it is slower than a salted ice bath and much less forgiving. A typical home freezer runs at about minus 18 °C. A can goes from room temperature to cold in perhaps 25 to 40 minutes, depending on the freezer and how full it is.

Wrapping each can or bottle in a wet paper towel speeds things up, because the water conducts heat better than air. Whatever you do, set a timer on your phone. Beer at around 5% ABV starts to freeze a degree or two below 0 °C. Water expands by about 9% when it freezes, so a forgotten bottle can crack or burst and a can can split or bulge.

Even when the container survives, partly frozen beer suffers. Ice crystals form from the water first, leaving a concentrated, sweeter liquid. Proteins can drop out as the beer thaws, leaving a haze or floating flakes. Carbonation can rush out when you open a half frozen can, giving a foaming mess and a flat beer.

A beer that froze and thawed is safe, but it often tastes thinner and duller. If you find a slushy can, let it thaw slowly in the fridge before opening. Do not expect it to taste as good as it should.

• Ice cubes in the glass. They water the beer down and kill the head. A thirsty party guest may not mind, but your craft beer deserves better.
  • A frozen glass. It foams the beer and adds freezer smells. Our guide on frozen glasses explains why.
  • Shaking the bucket. Turning cans gently helps. Shaking them hard makes them foam when opened.
  • Opening the freezer every two minutes. Each opening lets warm air in and slows the chill.

Most pale lagers taste best around 3 to 7 °C. Pale ales and wheat beers are happier at 6 to 10 °C. Stouts and strong ales at 10 to 14 °C. A salted ice bath can push a can below 0 °C if you leave it long enough, so take the beers out once they reach your target and move them to the fridge or a cooler with plain ice and water. Our guide to beer serving temperature gives more detail by style.

Overchilling is a real problem in Indian homes and bars. Ice cold beer numbs the palate, so a good craft beer tastes of far less than it should.

The best fix is to have beer in the fridge before you need it. If space is short, keep a few cans of each beer you plan to serve cold and put the rest in a cooler of ice water an hour before guests arrive. Buying beer from a shop that sells it chilled also saves time, as long as you get it home quickly in a cool bag.

Fill a bucket with ice and water, stir in salt and drop the cans in. Set a 12 minute timer, turn them once halfway through and check one by touch. That is your fastest route to cold beer without a burst bottle in the freezer.
faqs: What is the fastest way to chill beer?
A bucket of ice, water and salt. The water surrounds each can and the salt lets the bath go below 0 °C, so cans chill in about 10 to 15 minutes.
How long does beer take to chill in the freezer?
Usually about 25 to 40 minutes for a can, depending on the freezer. Set a timer so it does not freeze.
Can beer freeze in the freezer?
Yes. Most beers start to freeze a degree or two below 0 °C. Bottles can crack and cans can split if left too long.
Is beer safe to drink after it freezes?
Yes, it is safe, but it often tastes thinner and may be hazy or flat once thawed.
